title: Digital-analog concept for superconducting perceptron-like neural networks
authors: Andrey E. Schegolev, Vsevolod I. Ruzhickiy, Georgy I. Gubochkin, Alexander S. Ionin, Ivan A. Nazhestkin, Mikhail Y. Fominskii, Lyudmila V. Filippenko, Igor I. Soloviev, Maxim V. Tereshonok, Nikolay V. Klenov
abstract: A promising route to superconducting artificial neural networks is a hybrid digital-Analog architecture that combines digital single-flux-quantum (SFQ) communication with compact Analog nonlinear processing. The study focused on the dynamic conversion of a discrete signal passing through a digital-to-Analog-to-digital (DAD) converter, in which the role of the Analog cell was performed by a $Σ$-neuron with a nonlinear transfer function -- the basic cell of perceptron-like neural networks. Furthermore, the DAD converter, the elementary functional block of the hybrid architecture, combines a digital-to-analog converter (DAC) and an Analog-to-digital converter (ADC), and re-encodes the Analog $Σ$-neuron waveforms as an SFQ pulse sequence. Circuit-level simulations demonstrate how input values encoded by SFQ pulse trains are converted into analog signal levels, transformed by the $Σ$-neuron, and mapped back to pulse-based outputs. As a key experimental step, we fabricated and characterised a redesigned $Σ$-neuron and measured a sigmoid-like transfer characteristic suitable for activation-function implementation. The extracted response was incorporated into system-level simulations to assess the influence of realistic device parameters on the conversion process. We delineate the operating-range matching requirements for the DAC, neuron, and ADC blocks, supporting the feasibility of the proposed interface as a building block for perceptron-like superconducting neural networks with digital inputs and outputs. Finally, we developed two perceptron networks, one using a mathematical sigmoid activation and the other the measured $Σ$-neuron transfer characteristic, which reached classification accuracies of $97.0\%$ and $91.9\%$, respectively, on the MNIST handwritten digit dataset.
summary: This work proposes a superconducting neural network architecture that bridges the gap between digital SFQ logic and analog nonlinear processing using a $\Sigma$-neuron. By fabricating and characterizing this hybrid DAD converter, the authors demonstrate that the system can achieve high classification accuracy on MNIST, validating the feasibility of superconducting neuromorphic hardware.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of building energy-efficient superconducting artificial neural networks by proposing a hybrid digital-analog architecture.
main_result: They successfully demonstrated that a perceptron trained using the measured, non-ideal $\Sigma$-neuron characteristic achieved high classification accuracy (91.9%) on the MNIST dataset.
method: The study combines circuit-level simulations with physical device characterization, fabricating and measuring a $\Sigma$-neuron to validate its use in a full digital-analog-digital (DAD) processing chain.
model_or_system: The core system is a superconducting perceptron utilizing Single-Flux-Quantum (SFQ) communication for digital I/O, coupled with an analog $\Sigma$-neuron for nonlinear processing. The architecture is modeled as a DAC $ightarrow$ $\Sigma$-neuron $ightarrow$ ADC chain.
key_observables: Classification accuracies on MNIST (97.0% for ideal sigmoid vs. 91.9% for measured $\Sigma$-neuron); the measured sigmoid-like transfer characteristic of the $\Sigma$-neuron.
important_parameters: Operating range matching requirements for DAC, neuron, and ADC blocks; Josephson junction parameters ($ eta, \alpha, b, a$).
main_assumptions: The approach assumes the $\Sigma$-neuron can serve as the constrained nonlinear element, and that individual blocks can be simulated and integrated despite not being co-simulated as a single self-consistent circuit.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the conceptual DAD path (DAC + $\Sigma$-neuron + ADC), the specific superconducting circuit elements (DFF, TFF), and the simulation results showing the conversion process and final network performance.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the need for a hybrid architecture, detailing the circuit models for the digital (SFQ) and analog ($\Sigma$-neuron) components, presenting the characterization of the fabricated $\Sigma$-neuron, and concluding with system-level simulations and performance testing on MNIST.
why_interesting: While focused on superconducting electronics, the underlying principles of using nonlinear dynamics ($\Sigma$-neuron) to model complex computation and the integration of physical constraints into machine learning models resonate with the study of non-equilibrium dynamics in complex systems.
